How scoring works

Scoring method

×

Equal evidence earns equal scores

Every category orders its underlying assessments across all 57 cars, then places each group of equal values by its midpoint percentile: (number strictly better + half the tied group) / cohort count. Bands at 20%, 40%, 60% and 80% receive +2, +1, 0, −1 and −2 from highest to lowest; exact boundaries go toward zero. Groups stay together, so band sizes vary and some bands can be empty. Category ranks are shared. Adding a candidate can change relative tiers; these are shortlist comparisons, not absolute quality ratings.

Total = sum of each category score × its allocated points. Each active category adds one point to the shared budget; turning it off removes one point. Sliders run from off to two points (twice the default), with one point at the center. Changing an active slider redistributes the remainder proportionally, capping every category at two points and sharing any excess among the others. Every category can be turned off. Five categories start at one point each; Maintenance starts off. Tiers remain fixed while allocations change. Equal totals sort by lower five-year cost, then name. With all categories off, totals are zero and cars sort by cost. Reset restores defaults.

Every car receives a numeric assessment for every metric. Where exact evidence is incomplete, the best available proxy or editorial estimate is used, with its basis in the details. A zero is a middle-band result. Uncertainty does not introduce a separate bonus or penalty.

Pareto paths

A direct upgrade is no worse on every active tier and better on at least one, with no intermediate score profile between the two. Equal profiles share a node. Each layer removes the remaining non-dominated profiles. The preferred path repeatedly chooses the lowest-scoring direct dominator; equal totals break by calculated five-year cost, then name. This tie-break is display order, not an additional dominance metric.

All 57 cars participate, including those with proxy estimates. Rankings, Pareto comparisons and research dialogs use the same five-level scores calculated across the full cohort. Positive weight changes cannot change dominance; turning a metric on or off can. More levels expose more tradeoffs, not more precise evidence.

Ownership: one visible five-year calculation

New dealer-purchased EVs are exempt from the $121 Road Improvement Fee at initial registration; the four renewals include it. Pickup weight fees are included as explicit annual bracket allowances; exact registered weight needs a dealer/DMV quote. Five-year costs are scenarios: resale, insurance, fuel rates and charging prices can change the order. See the full scoring audit and sensitivity table.

New vehicles of any body style, estimated at or below $60,000 out the door in Orange County. Prices use the named model year and configuration, published MSRP, destination and selected packages. No assumed dealer discount, markup or contingent rebate. MSRP in the breakdown excludes destination so it is added exactly once. A published US configuration is not a claim of current stock at a particular dealer. Model years may overlap during the sales year.

Five-year cost = OTD − resale + gasoline + electricity + four registration renewals + insurance + routine upkeep + repair reserve + selected assistance subscriptions. Financing is excluded. First registration and sales tax appear once, inside OTD. Roof carriers and winter tires are extra for every vehicle; no carrier purchase is assumed in the base cost.

Common scenario: 12,000 miles/year for five years; 7.75% Irvine sales tax baseline (other OC cities differ); $85 taxable document fee; current DMV registration/CHP/TIF/VLF schedules plus a $30 annual county-fee allowance. Renewal value factors are 90%, 80%, 70%, 60% of purchase price, explicit planning approximations rather than a DMV calculation. EV road fees are included. Rates are held constant for this comparison.

Nearby public charging is assumed available at ordinary local electricity cost, $0.344/kWh, with no installation charge, availability penalty or retail charging markup, as requested. This is a comparison assumption, not a posted public-station tariff. Gasoline is held at the checked OC AAA reference: $5.5049 regular / $5.9038 premium per gallon. The EPA record’s fuel grade is costed; premium-fuel references do not establish that regular is prohibited. EPA wall-energy consumption already includes charging losses; none are added twice.

PHEVs use a disclosed 60% electric-mile scenario and 40% gasoline miles; this assumes regular access to charging and is not an EPA prediction for your driving. Gas-mode MPG and electrical consumption are separate. Resale uses the identified historical model or segment depreciation benchmark; new generations/powertrains use segment assumptions, not invented exact-build forecasts. The applied fraction and its scope appear in each Cost assessment.

Insurance is a common $2,500/year allowance, not a personalized or model-specific quote. Routine upkeep allowances are 10¢/mile gas, 9¢ hybrid/PHEV, and 6¢ EV, including tires. Repairs add a common $200/year reserve. These round planning inputs are not measured 2026 expenses; the DOE study supports the maintenance-cost distinction, not these exact allowances. Resale and insurance are substantial uncertainties; compare quotes and sensitivity before a purchase.

Comfort includes the liftgate

40% ride/noise + 30% seating + 20% cabin ergonomics + 10% assessed power liftgate. Each component is 0–5; a selected power liftgate assessed as present earns 5 on that component and a manual opening earns 0. Automatic trunk unlatching alone is not a powered liftgate. Body style and power liftgate never determine eligibility. Comfort does not include driver assistance.

Ride, noise and seating judgments are editorial estimates based on the named configuration’s equipment and packaging, not instrumented road tests. A luxury badge, screen size or trim price does not independently establish comfort. Notes identify the tradeoffs; small component differences need a test drive.

Ride/noise uses a shared 3/5 baseline without comparable exact-configuration road tests. EV propulsion, luxury branding, price and wheel size alone earn no bonus or penalty. Seating and control scores remain editorial equipment/preference estimates, with four separate component explanations for every car. A powered hatch is convenience, not a measured quietness or seating benefit.

Eco: historical lifecycle anchors and best estimates

ACEEE Green Scores consider manufacturing, energy supply, use and disposal impacts. Published US coverage ends at model year 2024. 20 retained assessments use comparable historical configurations and preserve their original source records. They are historical comparison anchors, not measured current-model results.

The other 37 assessments are editorial lifecycle proxies on the same 0–100 comparison scale. Prefer a historical configuration in the same model family and powertrain, then a similar vehicle class; current efficiency, packaging and battery changes inform coarse adjustments. Each detail names the proxy models, their published scores and the adjustment rationale. Redesigns and different models receive estimates rather than purported exact published ratings.

The ownership-cost assumption of 60% electric PHEV miles does not recalculate a historical lifecycle score. Charging habits affect real-world impacts. No direct MPG-versus-MPGe comparison or mixing of European Green NCAP scores is used. Efficient use-phase consumption alone is not a full lifecycle assessment. Proxy values incorporate judgment and remain approximate; five-level tiers do not imply additional measurement precision.

ACEEE lifecycle methodology ↗ GreenerCars coverage notice ↗ Green NCAP lifecycle assessments ↗

Proxy convention: retain a named historical reference without an invented efficiency or redesign adjustment; when multiple references are retained, use their unadjusted arithmetic mean. This convention makes the estimate reproducible but does not validate the chosen comparators or create a current-model lifecycle result. Same-model/powertrain references take priority where established. Historical reference scores remain unchanged.

Mountain trips: three adults and their gear

40% carrying usefulness + 35% winter access + 25% trip practicality. Assess two front occupants, one rear adult, bags and long ski/snowboard gear. Maximum cargo with every rear seat folded does not prove fit. Sedan access and low clearance affect usefulness; AWD alone does not prove good winter tires or stopping ability.

Carrying estimates use the manufacturer’s packaging evidence, with verified dimensions where available. Gear fit is unmeasured. Roof routes remain conditional on exact roof, bars/feet, load rating, carrier capacity and clearance. Roof loads add drag, height and handling/loading costs. Current EV range and charging hardware inform trip estimates, without claiming an exact cold-weather or roof-load range penalty.

Trip practicality uses a provisional 3/5 EV baseline until a sourced assessment of loaded winter range, arrival reserve and charging stops supports a higher input. EPA range or peak charging power alone does not establish that upgrade. EVs can earn higher inputs with that evidence; there is no fixed EV tier cap. Gas, hybrid and PHEV builds receive 5/5 for rapid liquid-fuel replenishment, not for overall trip excellence. Carrying and winter access are separate. No exact winter-range percentage or charging wait is assumed.

Carrying scores are packaging estimates, not verified ski/board fit. Winter access reflects the selected drivetrain and clearance; AWD does not establish braking grip. A +2 is relative to this cohort, not a guarantee of suitability for a particular route.

Commute assistance: selected equipment, not options you did not buy

40% traffic/speed control + 35% steering coverage + 25% supervision/usability. Each selected system has its own component rationale. Traffic/speed 4 means ordinary stop/go following; 5 adds supported route-aware speed or intersection handling. Steering 0 means corrective support only, 3 means speed-limited centering, 4 means ordinary continuous centering, and 5 adds assisted lane changes or route turns. Supervision/usability 3 is the hands-on baseline; 4 credits documented attention-monitoring or coordinated driver-inactivity response. These are editorial capability estimates, not independent performance scores. A lane-departure warning or corrective lane-keeping system receives no continuous-centering credit. A manual describing optional equipment does not prove trim fitment. Where fitment evidence is incomplete, use the best estimate for the selected grade and explain it in the details; optional equipment is not automatically credited.

Costs include selected assistance options and any credited paid subscription over five years; temporary trials do not establish permanent entitlement. Unselected hands-free upgrades receive no credit. Honda/Acura lane-centering operating speeds, restart behavior and other system limits remain important. These are capability estimates, not independent performance or safety ratings; IIHS safeguards ratings are not steering-quality scores.

Maintenance evidence and uncertainty

50% fewer disruptions + 30% less routine service effort + 20% service access. This is a low-confidence editorial comparison and starts off. Evidence confidence is shown separately and never enters the calculation. Without applicable failure evidence, every vehicle uses the same 3/5 disruption baseline; neither a redesign nor a new powertrain is penalized, and age or brand reputation alone earns no reliability bonus. Service access also uses a shared 3/5 baseline without a local shop census. Gas, hybrid and PHEV routine effort shares a 3/5 baseline because comparable schedule/time evidence has not established a difference; no PHEV complexity penalty is applied. EVs receive 5/5 routine effort for fewer scheduled engine-related tasks in the DOE framework, while tires, brakes and other service remain. These are disclosed estimates, not exact-build maintenance schedules.

Dollar service and repair allowances are already in Cost. This category emphasizes time, effort and disruption, so consider overlap when weighting it. RepairPal describes a historical methodology; the components here are not RepairPal ratings, a local shop census, failure probabilities or numeric repairability scores.

RepairPal reliability methodology ↗

Editorial component rubric

0 = assessed as absent; 1 = very constrained; 2 = constrained; 3 = workable baseline; 4 = useful capability with caveats; 5 = unusually strong fit. Each assessment shows its inputs and rationale. Estimated fitment is identified with its evidence and rationale; it is distinct from verified equipment. Capability components describe planning usefulness, not laboratory results or failure rates. No hidden confidence bonus or penalty is applied.

Audit and evidence limitations

37 Crossover · 9 Hatchback · 3 Minivan · 2 Pickup · 6 Sedan. 10 EV · 18 Gas · 25 Hybrid · 4 PHEV.

Representative market comparison: 57 ranked configurations from 73 screened candidates. The field adds minivans, compact pickups and larger family SUVs alongside sedans and hatchbacks, without quotas or a fixed count. It is not an exhaustive market inventory. Outback and Crown Signia retain their manufacturer SUV classification; no verified new assisted wagon under the budget was established. Every removed and newly screened candidate is documented in the audit report. Remaining gaps include dealer quotes, individual insurance, actual gear fit, future resale and current-model lifecycle/reliability measurements.

Source dates and scope appear with each configuration. The comparison, details and sliders work offline; external evidence links need a network.

Mountain trips

+1Upper band · #23 of 57 assessed

Editorial three-adult planning estimate

Three adults + gear: Useful crossover packaging and AWD/8.3-inch clearance support carrying and winter-access estimates. Those strengths do not establish easy long-distance winter travel; trip practicality uses the same provisional EV baseline as its peers.

Interior: Unmeasured: retain one rear adult plus boots/bags and check a partial seat-fold/pass-through against actual ski/board dimensions. Published cargo volume alone does not establish fit.

Roof route: Candidate carrier route is unverified: confirm exact roof option, feet/bars, dynamic load, carrier capacity and hatch/trunk clearance before purchase. No roof equipment is assumed included.

Winter: AWD/4WD traction and clearance help access, but selected tires are not assumed to be winter-rated. Carry compliant chains and check the manual.

Trip: 2026 Premium EPA reference: 288 miles. Subaru advertises about 28 minutes for 10–80% DC charging, battery preconditioning and NACS compatibility. These improve on the predecessor but do not establish loaded winter range, charger availability or stop duration on the intended route. Cold, climbing, gear and roof drag reduce usable range.

Carrying: 4/5: Useful crossover or pickup carrying estimate; long-gear geometry and remaining adult space still need a physical check. Selected configuration: Premium AWD, 18-inch wheels. This is an editorial packaging estimate, not a measured fit.

Winter access: 4/5: Selected AWD and higher-clearance configuration support the strongest access estimate here; this is not a stopping-distance or winter-tire rating. EPA drivetrain: All-Wheel Drive. Winter tires and compliant traction devices are not assumed included.

Trip practicality: 3/5: provisional EV replenishment baseline. The selected build has a 288-mile EPA reference, not a loaded winter range measurement. No route-specific winter range, reserve and charging-stop assessment establishes a higher rating; range alone does not earn one. Charging speed, compatibility and reliability at the actual stops still matter.

Trip inputs reviewed 2026-11-15 across the full cohort. Carrying, winter access and replenishment are distinct judgments. Exact gear fit and route-specific performance remain unverified; no extra brand, AWD or redesign bonus is applied.

Rack/box and winter tires cost extra and are excluded from the base cost comparison for every vehicle. Exact gear fit, roof load and hatch/trunk clearance remain unmeasured.

Editorial inputs: Carrying 4/5 (40%) · Winter access 4/5 (35%) · Trip practicality 3/5 (25%). Composite 3.75/5.

Evidence: 2026 · Premium AWD, 18-inch wheels.

Comfort

+1Upper band · #15 of 57 assessed

Editorial equipment/packaging estimate

Premium includes StarTex upholstery, a power driver seat and a conventional power rear gate. Limited kick activation and higher-seat features are excluded. Ride/noise remains at the shared 3/5 baseline.

Selected configuration has a verified power liftgate. Liftgate is 10% of Comfort only; body style never determines eligibility. Assistance is separate.

Ride/noise: 3/5: shared ride/noise baseline. EV propulsion, price, brand, wheel size and acoustic equipment alone do not quantify the combined ride/noise result; compare the exact tires, road and test conditions before changing it.

Seating: 3/5: editorial selected-seat equipment/support estimate. Ordinary seating receives the workable baseline; heated fronts or a power driver seat alone do not prove superior support for all occupants. Rear-adult space and personal fit need a seat test.

Cabin ergonomics: 3/5: editorial controls estimate. Workable controls baseline; no measured task-time or distraction result is claimed.

Power liftgate: 5/5: Premium includes a conventional power rear gate. Limited adds kick activation; that higher-grade feature is not credited.

Reviewed 2026-11-15: equipment convenience and control preferences are distinguished from measured comfort. No brand or propulsion-based ride/noise bonus or penalty is applied.

Maintenance

+2Highest band · #1 of 57 assessed

Editorial upkeep estimate; confidence separate

Disruption uses the shared 3/5 baseline because applicable current-model failure evidence has not been established. Neither redesign/new-powertrain status nor brand reputation changes that baseline. Service access is held equal without a local shop census.

Evidence confidence (not scored): Low: current-model disruption and local service access are not measured. Routine-service direction has stronger powertrain-level evidence than model-specific reliability.

Less disruption: 3/5: shared disruption baseline. Historical continuity alone is not measured reliability, and missing data is not evidence of more failures.

Less routine upkeep: 5/5: the DOE maintenance framework supports fewer scheduled engine-related tasks for battery EVs. Tires, brakes, filters, fluids and inspections remain; this is a powertrain-level effort estimate, not an exact-build maintenance schedule.

Service access: 3/5: shared service-access baseline; no local repair-network census or quantified parts-delay evidence supports a model-specific adjustment.

EV scheduled work avoids engine oil/ignition/exhaust service but still includes tires, brakes, filters, fluids and inspections.

Repairability: Parts, diagnostic subscriptions, collision/high-voltage access and battery/component repair procedures require a vehicle-specific check. No numerical repairability rating is assigned.

No current-model failure rate or numeric repairability rating is claimed. Dollar upkeep is already in Cost; this dimension concerns time and disruption.

Editorial inputs: Less disruption 3/5 (50%) · Less routine upkeep 5/5 (30%) · Service access 3/5 (20%). Composite 3.6/5.

Editorial three-adult planning estimate

Three adults + gear: Low-cost sedan with TSS 3.0 and 50 MPG. The conventional trunk and rear-adult space constrain three-person long-gear trips without excluding the car.

Roof route: Candidate carrier route is unverified: confirm exact roof option, feet/bars, dynamic load, carrier capacity and hatch/trunk clearance before purchase. No roof equipment is assumed included.

Winter: Selected two-wheel-drive build needs appropriate winter tires/chains and a clearance check; traction equipment is not inferred from the body style.

Trip: Fuel stops are straightforward; loaded climbing, cold and roof drag raise consumption. No exact winter-trip range is claimed.

Carrying: 2/5: Restricted rear-adult/luggage packaging or sedan access limits three adults plus long gear. Selected configuration: LE FWD. This is an editorial packaging estimate, not a measured fit.

Winter access: 1/5: Low-clearance two-wheel-drive configuration limits access in snow. EPA drivetrain: Front-Wheel Drive. Winter tires and compliant traction devices are not assumed included.

Trip practicality: 5/5: rapid liquid-fuel replenishment baseline, not an overall mountain-trip rating. Fuel availability and consumption on the actual route still need checking; carrying and winter access are scored separately.

Trip inputs reviewed 2026-11-15 across the full cohort. Carrying, winter access and replenishment are distinct judgments. Exact gear fit and route-specific performance remain unverified; no extra brand, AWD or redesign bonus is applied.

Rack/box and winter tires cost extra and are excluded from the base cost comparison for every vehicle. Exact gear fit, roof load and hatch/trunk clearance remain unmeasured.

Steering coverage: 4/5: selected continuous lane centering covers ordinary highway following, with low-speed assistance where supported. It is supervised steering assistance; complex intersections and automatic lane changes are not credited.

Supervision/usability: 3/5: baseline supervised, hands-on operation and driver-facing status/alerts. A generic attention or drowsiness warning is not treated as camera-based gaze monitoring. No independent exact-build usability result is claimed.

Component values compare supported tasks and editorial usefulness. Road conditions, restart limits, software and driver supervision still matter. A higher capability score is not a safety certification.

+1Upper band · #14 of 57 assessed

Editorial three-adult planning estimate

Three adults + gear: Base RDX already has ACC, speed-limited LKAS and powered tailgate. No Technology-package price or acoustic-side-glass benefit is assumed. LKAS does not provide low-speed traffic-jam steering.

Interior: Unmeasured: retain one rear adult plus boots/bags and check a partial seat-fold/pass-through against actual ski/board dimensions. Published cargo volume alone does not establish fit.

Roof route: Candidate carrier route is unverified: confirm exact roof option, feet/bars, dynamic load, carrier capacity and hatch/trunk clearance before purchase. No roof equipment is assumed included.

Winter: AWD/4WD traction and clearance help access, but selected tires are not assumed to be winter-rated. Carry compliant chains and check the manual.

Trip: Fuel stops are straightforward; loaded climbing, cold and roof drag raise consumption. No exact winter-trip range is claimed.

Carrying: 4/5: Useful crossover or pickup carrying estimate; long-gear geometry and remaining adult space still need a physical check. Selected configuration: Base SH-AWD. This is an editorial packaging estimate, not a measured fit.

Winter access: 3/5: Selected AWD supports traction, with clearance/packaging limitations relative to the higher-clearance configurations. EPA drivetrain: All-Wheel Drive. Winter tires and compliant traction devices are not assumed included.

Trip practicality: 5/5: rapid liquid-fuel replenishment baseline, not an overall mountain-trip rating. Fuel availability and consumption on the actual route still need checking; carrying and winter access are scored separately.

Trip inputs reviewed 2026-11-15 across the full cohort. Carrying, winter access and replenishment are distinct judgments. Exact gear fit and route-specific performance remain unverified; no extra brand, AWD or redesign bonus is applied.

Rack/box and winter tires cost extra and are excluded from the base cost comparison for every vehicle. Exact gear fit, roof load and hatch/trunk clearance remain unmeasured.

Editorial inputs: Carrying 4/5 (40%) · Winter access 3/5 (35%) · Trip practicality 5/5 (25%). Composite 3.9/5.

Less routine upkeep: 5/5: the DOE maintenance framework supports fewer scheduled engine-related tasks for battery EVs. Tires, brakes, filters, fluids and inspections remain; this is a powertrain-level effort estimate, not an exact-build maintenance schedule.

Service access: 3/5: shared service-access baseline; no local repair-network census or quantified parts-delay evidence supports a model-specific adjustment.

EV scheduled work avoids engine oil/ignition/exhaust service but still includes tires, brakes, filters, fluids and inspections.

Repairability: Parts, diagnostic subscriptions, collision/high-voltage access and battery/component repair procedures require a vehicle-specific check. No numerical repairability rating is assigned.

No current-model failure rate or numeric repairability rating is claimed. Dollar upkeep is already in Cost; this dimension concerns time and disruption.

Editorial inputs: Less disruption 3/5 (50%) · Less routine upkeep 5/5 (30%) · Service access 3/5 (20%). Composite 3.6/5.

10 vehicles share this underlying value and receive the same tier and category rank.

Evidence: Historical DOE maintenance framework; selected configuration context · LT1 FWD.
